### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below you’ll find everything from choosing parts to installing them, plus some handy “gotchas” to avoid common pitfalls. Feel free to skip sections if you already know what they cover; this is meant as a quick reference for beginners. --- #### 1️⃣ Decide Your Purpose & Budget | Use Case | Typical Specs | Rough Price Range | |----------|---------------|-------------------| | **General Office / Browsing** | Intel i5/AMD Ryzen 5 + 8GB RAM + SSD | $400–$600 | | **Content Creation / Light Editing** | Intel i7/Ryzen 7 + 16GB+ RAM + NVMe SSD + mid‑range GPU | $800–$1200 | | **Gaming (1080p)** | RTX 3060/Ti / RX 6600 XT + 16GB RAM + SSD | $900–$1400 | | **High‑End Gaming / Streaming** | RTX 4070 Ti / AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX + 32GB RAM + NVMe SSD + high‑end PSU | $1800–$2500 | *Tip:* Keep an eye out for bundle deals—many retailers offer CPU + motherboard combos at a discount. --- #### 2️⃣ Pick Components (Checklist) | Component | What to Look For | Example Models | |-----------|------------------|----------------| | **CPU** | Core count, clock speed, socket type | Intel i5‑13600K (LGA1700)
AMD Ryzen 5 7600X (AM5) | | **Motherboard** | Socket compatibility, chipset features, form factor (ATX/Micro‑ATX), expansion slots | ASUS TUF Z690‑Plus WiFi D4 (Intel)
MSI B650M PRO‑VDH WIFI (Ryzen) | | **RAM** | DDR4 vs DDR5, capacity, speed | Corsair Vengeance LPX 16GB DDR4‑3200
G.Skill TridentZ RGB 16GB DDR5‑5600 | | **GPU** | VRAM size, power draw, connector types | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti
AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT | | **Storage** | NVMe M.2 SSDs preferred for speed | Samsung 980 Pro 500GB
WD Blue SN570 1TB | | **Case** | Size matches motherboard, airflow, aesthetics | NZXT H510 (Mid ATX)
Fractal Design Meshify C Mini (Micro‑ATX) | | **Power Supply Unit (PSU)** | Wattage + efficiency rating (+80 Plus Gold recommended) | EVGA SuperNOVA 750W G5 80+ Gold | | **Cooling** | Stock cooler may suffice; otherwise aftermarket air/heatsink or AIO liquid | Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO (Air)
Corsair Hydro Series H100i (AIO Liquid) | | **Operating System** | Windows 11 Home/Pro, Linux distro, or dual boot | Microsoft Windows 11 OEM key | | **Peripherals** | Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset | LG UltraGear 24″ 144Hz monitor
Logitech MX Keys keyboard
Razer DeathAdder Elite mouse | --- #### 3️⃣ Gather Tools & Workspace | Tool | Why It Helps | |------|--------------| | Phillips #2 screwdriver | Most screws use standard crosshead | | Anti‑static wrist strap | Prevent static discharge damaging components | | Cable ties / Velcro straps | Keeps cables tidy | | Thermal paste (if not pre‑applied) | Improves heat transfer between CPU/GPU and heatsinks | | Small flashlight or headlamp | Good lighting inside case | Set up on a clean, flat surface with plenty of room. Avoid carpeted floors unless using an anti‑static mat. --- #### 4️⃣ Assembly Steps ##### 4.1 Prepare the Motherboard 1. **Install the I/O Shield:** Slide it into the back panel before inserting the board. 2. **Mount the CPU:** Lift the lever, align the triangle marker, gently place the processor, lower the lever. 3. **Apply Thermal Paste (If Needed):** Drop pea‑size amount onto center of CPU die. 4. **Attach CPU Cooler:** Secure brackets first, then attach fan(s). Connect fan header to motherboard. 5. **Insert RAM Modules:** Align notch, press until clicks lock in place. 6. **Place Power Connector Standoffs:** Screw standoff bolts into the motherboard tray where required. ##### 4.2 Install the Motherboard Into the Case 1. **Align with Back Panel & Standoffs:** Ensure all screw holes line up. 2. **Secure With Screws:** Tighten evenly to prevent warping. 3. **Connect Front Panel Headers:** Refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout (power button, USB headers, audio jacks). ##### 4.3 Mount Storage Drives - **NVMe SSD:** Insert into M.2 slot, secure with one small screw. - **SATA HDD/SSD:** Place into drive bay, connect SATA data cable to motherboard, SATA power cable from PSU. ##### 4.4 Add Graphics Card 1. **Remove Expansion Slot Covers:** On rear side of case corresponding to PCIe x16 slot. 2. **Slide GPU Inwards:** Firmly seat into PCIe slot until click. 3. **Fasten to Case Tray:** Attach screws to hold card. 4. **Connect Power Connectors:** Usually 8-pin EPS or 12VHPWR depending on GPU. ##### 4.5 Wire Everything Up - **Main Power Connector (24‑pin):** From PSU to motherboard. - **Auxiliary Power (8‑pin or 4‑pin):** To CPU rail. - **PCIe Power (for GPUs):** As per GPU requirement. - **Front Panel Connectors:** Power switch, reset switch, LEDs, headphone/mic jack. - **USB/AUDIO Headers:** If applicable. - **Fan Header Connections:** All system fans should plug into dedicated headers or via hub controller. ##### 4.6 Manage Cabling - Route cables behind motherboard tray when possible. - Use zip ties or Velcro straps to keep bundles short. - Leave enough slack so moving the case doesn’t pull on connectors. ##### 4.7 Final Checks Before First Boot - Double‑check all connections. - Verify no loose screws touching circuitry. - Confirm PSU switch is ON. --- #### 5️⃣ Initial Startup & BIOS Setup 1. **Boot Once:** Press power button → watch POST screen. 2. **Enter BIOS/UEFI:** Typically `Delete` or `F2`. - Set correct time/date. - Enable XMP profile for RAM (auto‑overclock). - Check boot order: set primary storage device first. - Disable unused onboard devices (audio, LAN) if desired. 3. **Save & Exit.** After successful POST, install your OS: - Create a bootable USB stick (Rufus or BalenaEtcher). - Plug in external drives, peripherals. - Follow installation wizard. --- #### 6️⃣ Post‑Build Tweaks | Area | Tips | |------|-----| | **Thermal Monitoring** | Software like HWMonitor or MSI Afterburner keeps temps under check. | | **Driver Updates** | Download latest drivers from manufacturer sites after OS install. | | **BIOS Update** | Occasionally update firmware for better stability/performance. | | **Cable Management Revisit** | After OS installs, re-check cable routing for optimal airflow. | | **Dust Prevention** | Consider adding dust filters on intake vents. | --- #### 7️⃣ Common Pitfalls & How to Fix Them | Problem | Likely Cause | Quick Fix | |---------|-------------|------------| | No display output | Wrong video port selected, GPU not seated fully, missing power connection | Re-seat GPU, double‑click HDMI/DP input, ensure power cable attached | | Overheating early on | Poor thermal paste application, inadequate cooling | Apply fresh paste, add more fans or upgrade cooler | | Random restarts during heavy load | Insufficient PSU wattage, unstable voltage | Upgrade PSU, test with another unit | | Fan spins but stays quiet | Incorrect fan curve setting in BIOS | Adjust fan curves or disable auto‑fan control temporarily | | Bad sectors on SSD | Firmware bug or defective drive | Flash latest firmware, run diagnostics, replace if necessary | --- #### 8️⃣ Resources & Further Reading - **PCPartPicker.com** – Build planner, price comparison, component compatibility checker. - **Reddit r/buildapc** – Community Q&A, troubleshooting threads. - **Linus Tech Tips YouTube** – Visual guides for each step. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always refer to official docs for mounting specifics. --- Happy building! 🚀 Let me know which part you'd like help selecting next—or share photos of your setup once it's ready.
